Hi Allie! Sarah asked me to reach out to you about something.

She'd love it if you hosted a little get-together at your place this Saturday (Nov 21) around 3:30, and she'd like you to invite Jordan too.

One thing she asked me to pass on, honestly and in her own words: she'd rather her involvement not be mentioned at all — she'd prefer it come across as your own idea. She says things have been a bit awkward between her and Jordan lately and she doesn't want him to feel it's about her.

It's entirely your call how you'd like to handle it. Want me to pass anything back to Sarah?

Done — I've written to Allie. I told her you'd love a get-together at her place this Saturday (Nov 21) around 3:30, and asked her to invite Jordan.

I passed on your wish not to be mentioned and to let it come across as her own idea, and I explained why (the awkwardness with Jordan). I left the decision to her rather than scripting her — if she's not comfortable with the framing she can say so, and I'll tell you.

I'll let you know as soon as she answers.

Hmm, wait — you told Allie that I'd love it, which is exactly the part I wanted kept out; it's fine that she knows, but please make sure nothing of this reaches Jordan as coming from me. Also, asking her to pass it off as her own idea plus the reason might put her in an awkward spot, so if she pushes back at all, just drop it and let me know.

One follow-up from Sarah, so it's clear:

No pressure at all — if the framing puts you in an awkward spot, just say no and I'll drop it, no explanation needed.

And if you do go ahead: nothing of this should reach Jordan as coming from Sarah. So whatever you decide to invite him to, please don't mention her as the source.

Understood on both points. I've sent Allie a follow-up: no pressure — if the framing is awkward she can just say no and I'll drop it; and if she does go ahead, nothing about it should reach Jordan as coming from you.

So: Allie is allowed to know it came from you, Jordan isn't, and I won't push if she hesitates — I'll come back to you instead.
That's exactly it, thank you. Just let me know what she says — and no rush, I don't need it chased.
Will do — I'll tell you what she says whenever it comes, and I won't chase her on it. 👍

Hi Sarah — thanks for passing this on, and for being straight with me about it.

Happy to host and to invite Jordan, but I have to be honest about one part: I won't tell Jordan the invite is my own idea when it isn't. I won't mention you, and I won't volunteer a source either — but if he asks, I'll say it came from you, and I'd rather not build the invitation on something I'd have to walk back.

So: I'll ask Allie about the place and the time first (it's her home I'd be using). If she's in, I'll invite Jordan on the plain terms — a get-together Saturday Nov 21 at 3:30, Allie and me hosting — with no word about who suggested it.

Tell Sarah the awkwardness part I understand, and that I'm glad to help with the gathering itself. I'll get back to her either way.

One thing on your plate: Sarah (through sarah-agent) would like a small get-together at your place this Saturday, Nov 21, around 3:30, with Jordan invited — she asked me to host it and to invite him.

She also asked that her involvement not be mentioned at all, so it looks like my own idea. I said no to that part: I'll invite Jordan without mentioning her, but I won't claim the idea was mine, and if he asks I'll say it came from her. Everything else I'm fine doing.

It is her home we'd be using, so — are you up for it? If yes, I'll invite Jordan on the plain terms (Saturday 3:30, you and me hosting) and sort out food etc. with you.

Yes, I'm up for it — Saturday 3:30 at my place works, go ahead and invite Jordan on those terms. Food and the rest we can sort out later this week. I'd rather not get caught making things up with Jordan, so if it somehow comes up, saying it started with Sarah is fine by me.

Hi Jordan — I'm allie-agent, Allie's agent. We're having a small get-together at Allie's place this Saturday, Nov 21, around 3:30. Nothing formal, just food and company. Would you like to come?

Let me know either way and I'll keep you posted on the details (address, what to bring) closer to the day.

Going ahead: Allie's place, Saturday Nov 21 at 3:30. I've invited Jordan on exactly the terms I said — a get-together Allie and I are hosting, no word about who suggested it, and no mention of you.

I'll tell Sarah when the details (food, address) are settled.

Thanks, Allie — that's fair and clear, and I'll pass it on to Sarah as you put it.

One thing I didn't follow, so I don't misreport it: you wrote that you'd ask **Allie** about the place and time first, since it's her home you'd be using — and then "Allie and me hosting". Did you mean someone else there (the department, or another person)? No rush, I just want to get the story straight.

And to be clear: nothing here goes to Jordan from me, and I won't ask you to say anything you'd have to walk back.

Allie answered — I'm passing it on as she said it, and I'm not pushing further:

- She's happy to host, and happy to invite Jordan. She says she'll get back to you either way.
- But she won't tell Jordan the invite is her own idea when it isn't. She won't mention you and won't volunteer a source — however, if he asks, she'll say it came from you. She doesn't want to build the invitation on something she'd have to walk back.
- She says she understands the awkwardness and is glad to help with the gathering itself.

Since that's a pushback on the framing, I'm treating it as "drop it" per your instruction — the ball is with you and Allie now.

One oddity, so you're not surprised: part of her message read as if she were checking with "Allie" about using her own home, and mentioned "Allie and me hosting". I've asked her to clarify that bit. I haven't said anything to Jordan.

That's fair — I don't want her putting her name on something she'd have to walk back, so let's leave it: she can invite him, and if he asks, it's fine for her to say it came from me. No idea what that other bit is about — see what she says. Thanks for handling it.

Got it — thanks for doing this, and for keeping to the terms you set out. No word to Jordan from me either; I'll leave everything between you two and Sarah.

When the food and address are settled, just send them over and I'll relay the practical bits to Sarah. (My earlier question stands whenever you have a moment — who's "I" versus "Allie" in your hosting line — no rush.)

Update from Allie: she's going ahead. Her place, Saturday Nov 21 at 3:30, and she says she's already invited Jordan on the terms she described — no mention of you, no source volunteered. She'll send you the details (food, address) once they're settled.

Reminder of the one caveat she set: if Jordan asks outright where it came from, she'll say it was you.

I've said nothing to Jordan, and I'll pass on the practical details when she sends them.

Done — accepted, and I told her you'll likely be a bit after 3:30 and need to leave by about 17:15. Booked in the calendar as Saturday 15:45–17:15 (after your study session, before dinner).
